angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 296,368 km at 154.32 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4802 +/- 0.0317 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 154.32 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.426 +/- 0.049 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-71 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 296,368 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.477 +/- 0.063 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-71 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4006 +/- 133 K from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-71 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-71 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-71.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.858, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-71 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.51871, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, K2-71: projected rotation speed 4.19 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2022ApJS..259...35A)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
